## 1. Blunt verdict
Byte-verified genuine mutant: `out3.srt` with byte 48 XORed by 0xFF (`'0' 0x30 → 0xCF`) — landing inside cue 2's start-time millisecond field (`00:10:00,00\xCF`). The name decodes exactly (xff3 = XOR-0xFF family, offset 048). The mutation makes the whole file invalid UTF-8, so parsing exercises the no-BOM Windows-1252 fallback (0xCF → 'Ï'), the unparseable ms field (BadTimestamp), and cue-2 survival semantics — three interesting paths in one byte. Consumer test `committed_corpus_survives` passes in baseline (cargo-test-workspace.txt:6113) with the per-run invariants (damage cap ≤256, valid intervals, cue count ≤ bytes).

## 2. Notes
- Coverage value: this is one of the 6 xff3 members (24-byte stride 000–144); the family and the 2000-round seeded loop together give reasonable fuzz-lite coverage of the encoding-fallback path.
- The generator script referenced by srt_fuzz_survival.rs:24-26 ("generated by a deterministic script") is NOT in the tree (scripts/ and tools/ have no SRT corpus generator) — the corpus is committed, so the run is reproducible, but corpus REGENERATION is not. S4-level note for the corpus as a whole, recorded here once; applies to crlf2.srt and flip2_072.srt identically.
